# 4 Ezra Chapter 5 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 5:5 — "blood shall drip from wood"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "blood shall-drip from-wood" | Literal — de ligno sanguis stillabit |
| LOGOS | "blood shall drip from wood" | Same without hyphens |
| PNEUMA | "Blood will drip from trees" | "Trees" interprets "wood" naturally |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Blood shall drip from wood" (LOGOS). "Wood" is more literal and preserves the strangeness of the sign.

---

## 5:9 — "fresh/salt water" inversion

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fresh-water shall-be-found-in-salt" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "salt water shall be found in fresh springs" | Reverses the clause for English idiom |
| PNEUMA | "Freshwater springs will turn brackish" | Paraphrase capturing the same reversal |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Salt water shall be found in fresh springs" (LOGOS). More precise about the location (springs) and more naturally readable.

---

## 5:22–26 — the election litany (vine/lily/river/Zion/dove/sheep/people)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | Hyphenated series, "you-chose" repeated | Preserves anaphoric structure literally |
| LOGOS | Clean parallel series with "you chose" | Formal and elegant |
| PNEUMA | Same structure with more variation per line | Readable but loses some parallelism |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS rendering throughout. The repeated "you chose / you named / you filled / you sanctified / you provided / you acquired" preserves the liturgical anaphora of the Latin.

---

## 5:41 — age made "for many" vs. "for the many"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "This-age the-Most-High-made for-many but-the age-to-come for-few" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "This age the Most High made for many, but the age to come for few" | Same in clean English |
| PNEUMA | "The Most High created this age for many, but the age to come for few" | Reverses subject/verb for fluency |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS. The word order "This age the Most High made" preserves the emphatic positioning of saeculum hoc in the Latin.

---

## 5:51 — left hand / right hand image

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "What-the-left-hand-covers is-more-than-what-the-right-hand-covers" | Full literal |
| LOGOS | "What the left hand covers exceeds what the right covers" | More elegant |
| PNEUMA | "what the left hand holds exceeds what the right holds" | Same with "holds" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "What the left hand holds exceeds what the right holds" — "holds" slightly clearer than "covers" while keeping the parallel structure.

---

## Total disagreements: 5
